annotation.title_clean: Outline for a normative and operational framework on emerging technologies in the area of lethal autonomous weapons systems
annotation.title_en: Outline for a normative and operational framework on emerging technologies in the area of lethal autonomous weapons systems
annotation.authors_or_issuer: France and Germany (submission to the CCW Group of Governmental Experts on LAWS)
annotation.venue: UN CCW Group of Governmental Experts on LAWS, working paper CCW/GGE.1/2021/WP.5
annotation.summary_en: Franco-German working paper to the CCW Group of Governmental Experts proposing a two-part normative and operational framework for lethal autonomous weapons systems. It builds on the 11 guiding principles, bans fully autonomous lethal systems outside human command, and requires human control, accountability, legal reviews, safeguards and a technical experts committee.
key_provisions_or_claims: HCPs commit not to develop or use fully autonomous lethal weapons operating outside human chain of command and control.
Human responsibility and accountability can never be transferred to machines and must be preserved across the life cycle.
Appropriate human control must cover understanding, monitoring reliability, defining rules of engagement and mission parameters, and judging IHL compliance.
Operational measures include legal weapons reviews, testing and certification, training, after-action review and prosecution of violations.
Safeguards include preventing diversion, cyber resilience, deactivation mechanisms, and a CCW technical experts committee.
